review_notes: I read the whole file and compared its definitions with Mathlib. I checked Quiver.SingleObj in Mathlib/Combinatorics/Quiver/SingleObj.lean. I grepped lean-pool's Kurosh and FiniteGraphFundamentalGroup directories for uses of Rose and roseQuiver. Rose is used only in SchreierCover.lean. I did not report coverQuiver. It is a deliberately different generator-labelled edge quiver on the same vertex type as the ActionCategory morphisms, so it is not the same concept as the group-element hom quiver. I did not report freeActionGroupoidIsFree, whose comment gives a reason for not using Mathlib's Nielsen–Schreier instance. I cannot compile, so I did not check whether the replacement elaborates. In particular, I did not check whether `Quiver.Star (Quiver.SingleObj.star α)` unfolds as smoothly as it does for `Rose.point`.

findings.excerpt:
inductive Rose (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | point : Rose α

instance roseQuiver (α : Type u) : Quiver (Rose α) where
  Hom _ _ := α
findings.problem: `Rose α` is a one-vertex quiver whose loops are the elements of `α`. Mathlib already has `Quiver.SingleObj α` for exactly this: the type tag on `Unit` with `Hom _ _ := α` and a distinguished vertex `Quiver.SingleObj.star α`. The file's own docstring describes `Rose` as 'The one-vertex quiver whose loops will be labeled by the generator type', so the two are the same concept under the same assumptions. The local copy gets none of Mathlib's API for this quiver. That API includes `toPrefunctor`, which turns maps `α → β` into prefunctors, `pathToList`/`pathEquivList`, and the reverse structure `hasReverse`. `Rose` is also a second, incompatible 'rose' notion alongside the library one. It is used only in this file, in `coverProjection`, `coverStarEquiv`, `coverCostarEquiv` and `coverProjection_isCovering`, so the change is local.
findings.proposed_change: Delete `Rose` and `roseQuiver`. Use `Quiver.SingleObj α` as the target of `coverProjection`, with `obj _ := Quiver.SingleObj.star α` and `map e := e.val`. Replace `Rose.point` by `Quiver.SingleObj.star α` in the `Quiver.Star` and `Quiver.Costar` statements. If the name is wanted, add `abbrev Rose := Quiver.SingleObj`.
findings.benefit: The module reuses the standard one-vertex quiver, so its covering statements and any prefunctor or path results compose with existing Mathlib API without conversions. The file drops a redundant inductive type and instance.
